findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with logical AND between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so a user must simultaneously be both team admin and team owner to pass, which is semantically wrong (should be OR) and means legitimate team admins-only or owners-only are denied access while the check silently falls through to isOrganizer/isAttendee, masking the authorization bug's blast radius. (confidence 100, severity P0)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-42 — booking is fetched via findFirst keyed only on id with no ownership/tenant predicate in the where clause, so the query shape itself carries no invariant tying booking access to the caller's tenant/org, pushing all authorization enforcement onto later imperative checks that must never be forgotten as the handler evolves. (confidence 75, severity P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-72 — blacklisted guest emails are read from process.env on every request instead of a cached config/settings source, coupling a per-request hot path to environment parsing and making the blacklist impossible to update without a process restart or to scope per-tenant. (confidence 75, severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 — EventManager is constructed with `{...user, credentials: [...credentials]}` where user is the raw session user object and credentials come from a separate getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) call, so the object shape fed to EventManager is assembled ad hoc at the call site rather than matching a defined UserWithCredentials contract, risking field drift (e.g. missing/duplicate `credentials` key shadowing, or divergence if `user` already had a `credentials` field) whenever either type changes upstream. (confidence 50, severity P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74-106 — uniqueGuests is deduplicated against the in-memory `booking.attendees` read at the top of the handler, then written via a separate createMany call with no unique constraint or transactional read-modify-write, so two concurrent addGuests calls for the same booking can both pass the dedup check against the same stale attendee snapshot and each insert the same guest email, producing duplicate attendee rows with no schema-level invariant preventing it. (confidence 75, severity P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — sendAddGuestsEmails failures are caught and only console.log'd after the DB write and calendar update already succeeded, so the email side effect is architecturally decoupled from the booking-state transition with no compensating action, retry queue, or surfaced status field, meaning the system has no record that guests were added without notification. (confidence 75, severity P2)

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests) takes no eventTypeMetadata parameter and never calls eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, so organizer/team/attendee emails are sent unconditionally even when the event type's disableStandardEmails.all.host or .attendee metadata flag is set, unlike every sibling function (sendScheduledEmails:99,111, sendRescheduledEmails:194,206, sendRoundRobinScheduledEmails:140, sendRoundRobinRescheduledEmails:158, sendRoundRobinCancelledEmails:176) which all gate on this flag. (confidence 90, P1)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — the call site `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` does not pass booking.eventType?.metadata (already fetched via the `eventType: true` include at line 32) even though the schema/metadata is available, so there is no way for the new code path to honor the disableStandardEmails toggle even if email-manager.ts were fixed to accept it. (confidence 85, P1)

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:539-547 — AttendeeAddGuestsEmail/AttendeeScheduledEmail are sent to every existing attendee in calendarEvent.attendees with no per-attendee opt-out check (e.g. no equivalent of hideOrganizerEmail or attendee-level notification preference), meaning any existing attendee who might be excluded from standard emails via event-type metadata still receives a guest-added notification.  (confidence 60, P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — email send failures are only console.log'd and swallowed, so there is no verification/telemetry that add-guest notifications actually reached the organizer/team/attendees, meaning a silent notification-delivery gap is unrecoverable and unobservable (no retry, no error reporting hook like other booking flows use).  (confidence 55, P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts — no workflow reminder trigger (e.g. scheduleWorkflowReminders equivalent used elsewhere on attendee changes) is invoked after guests are added, so any active reminder/notification workflows configured on the event type are not re-scheduled or updated to include the newly added guests. (confidence 50, P2)

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-58 — client-side validation only checks email format and uniqueness within the submitted batch; it does not check for duplicates against the booking's existing attendees (the backend silently filters these out via addGuests.handler.ts:74-78 producing a possible empty-after-filter list) nor surface the resulting BAD_REQUEST distinctly from a generic invalid-email error, so a user re-adding an existing attendee gets a confusing/generic failure instead of a clear "already invited" message.  (confidence 55, P2)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called on `EventManager` but no changes to `packages/core/EventManager` are included in this diff, so this method must already exist verbatim on that class or the build fails; it is not one of calcom's well-known EventManager methods (create/update/reschedule/updateLocation/cancelEvent), making its prior existence doubtful.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` is called with the full session-user object while the local variable `user` (identical to `ctx.user`) is used everywhere else in the function, so if the real `getUsersCredentials` signature expects a bare `userId: number` (as similarly-named helpers in `@calcom/lib/server/queries` do) this call passes the wrong argument type and fails to typecheck.

packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts:1 — `import { renderEmail } from "../"` and `import generateIcsString from "../lib/generateIcsString"` (also in organizer-add-guests-email.ts:3-4) resolve to `packages/emails/index.ts` and `packages/emails/lib/generateIcsString.ts`, neither of which exists anywhere in this repository snapshot, so this diff cannot be verified to compile even though the pattern matches other calcom templates by naming convention.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — Task commit (1081288) was authored 2026-09-13, three weeks after the "pr" commit (aeaf77e, 2026-08-24) that implements the change, so the task description describing "guest management" was written to retroactively document already-completed code rather than specify intent beforehand, meaning there is no original pre-implementation intent record to check the PR against, only a post-hoc label with no recorded human acceptance that the shipped scope satisfies it.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:22 — The task title says "guest management functionality" (implying create/update/remove) but the shipped handler (addGuestsHandler) only supports adding new guest emails to a booking's attendees list via createMany, with no update or delete/remove-guest capability anywhere in the diff, so the delivered scope is narrower than "management" and there is no recorded acceptance that "management" was intentionally reduced to "add-only".

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:1 — The UI artifact is named AddGuestsDialog (add-only) rather than a guest-management dialog (which would typically allow editing/removing existing attendees), reinforcing that the implementation targeted a narrower "add guests" feature than the task's "guest management" phrasing without any documented scope-narrowing decision.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-173 — after `prisma.booking.update` (line 92) has already committed new attendee rows, `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (line 165) is not wrapped in try/catch, so a thrown/rejected calendar-provider call bubbles as an unhandled exception (raw 500) while the guests remain persisted in the DB with no calendar invite and no notification email sent, producing SILENT-PARTIAL-SUCCESS/inconsistent state with no compensating action or rollback. Confidence 90, Severity P1.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:167-171 — `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` swallows email failures and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the client is told the operation fully succeeded even though calendar-invite/notification emails to attendees and organizer never went out. Confidence 95, Severity P1.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:169-170 — `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` logs a static string and never logs `err`, discarding the actual error message/stack, which removes the only debug signal for diagnosing email delivery failures in production. Confidence 90, Severity P3 (advisory).

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:528-549 — `sendAddGuestsEmails` fans out one `sendEmail` call per team member (line 532-536) plus one per attendee (line 539-547) via `Promise.all` with no cap on `calendarEvent.team.members` or `calendarEvent.attendees` length and no per-call timeout, so a booking with many guests/team members produces an unbounded N+M concurrent outbound email fan-out that can amplify a slow/failing mail provider into a large stalled request. Confidence 70, Severity P2.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:549 — `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)` rejects as soon as the first `sendEmail` call rejects, and that single rejection is what addGuests.handler.ts's catch swallows, meaning one bad recipient/provider hiccup can mask whether the other N emails in the batch actually succeeded or failed, since there's no `Promise.allSettled` or per-email status reporting back to the caller. Confidence 70, Severity P2.

packages/ui/index.tsx:153 — `export { default as MultiEmail } from "./form/MultiEmailLazy"` publishes a new generic component from the shared UI package's public API even though it has exactly one consumer (apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx), turning a feature-local input widget into a maintained shared-library surface (versioning/back-compat obligations) with no requirement in task-001.md calling for a reusable component. (confidence 90, severity P2)

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:1 — New 96-line generic multi-email-input component is added to packages/ui/form/ (shared package) rather than co-located in apps/web near AddGuestsDialog, expanding the shared package's scope beyond what "add guest management to bookings" requires. (confidence 75, severity P2)

packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx:1 — A second new file (lazy-loading wrapper) is added purely to support exporting MultiEmail from the shared package; this wrapper is only needed because the component was placed in the shared UI package instead of app-local, i.e. incidental scope generated by the index.tsx export decision rather than by any stated requirement. (confidence 70, severity P3)

docs/tasks/task-001.md:1 — Task title "Add guest management functionality" implies broader guest lifecycle (add/remove/edit) but the diff (addGuests.handler.ts, addGuests.schema.ts, AddGuestsDialog.tsx) implements add-only; the title overpromises relative to delivered scope, though the delivered add-only slice is itself internally consistent and not out-of-scope expansion. (confidence 60, severity P3)

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `isTeamAdminOrOwner = isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` uses logical AND instead of OR, so a user must simultaneously hold both the ADMIN and OWNER team roles (mutually exclusive in cal.com's membership model) to pass, meaning the team-admin/owner authorization branch is permanently unreachable; this fails closed (breaks the legitimate team-admin/owner "add guests" feature) rather than creating a bypass, since the overall authorization is `isTeamAdminOrOwner || isOrganizer || isAttendee` and isOrganizer/isAttendee remain correctly scoped to the actual booking — confidence 75, severity P3 (functional/authorization-availability bug, not an exploitable privilege escalation).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26-42 — `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } })` fetches any booking by id with no org/team/user scoping in the query itself, relying entirely on the later manual check (line 46-56) to enforce ownership; this is a latent IDOR risk pattern (defense only exists in application code, not the query), and if isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner ever throw, return true unexpectedly for a non-existent team (booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0 defaults to a fake team id 0), or if that later check is ever refactored/removed, any authenticated user could add guests to (and trigger emails/calendar updates for) an arbitrary booking they don't own — confidence 50, severity P2 (defense-in-depth gap, not currently confirmed exploitable since isOrganizer/isAttendee checks appear correctly scoped to booking.userId/attendees).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw, unvalidated-for-dedup `guests` input array (not the filtered `uniqueGuests`) into the email pipeline, where it is only used for an `.includes()` membership check (email-manager.ts:537) to select AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail templates, so no injection surface is created by this raw-array reuse, but it is inconsistent with the dedup/blacklist filtering applied everywhere else in the handler — confidence 50, severity P3 (advisory, not a vulnerability).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-72 — `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` env var is split naively on comma and lowercased, then compared via `.includes(guest)` against guest emails that are not lowercased before comparison, so a blacklisted email supplied with different casing (e.g. `Blocked@Example.com` vs configured `blocked@example.com`) bypasses the blacklist filter — confidence 75, severity P3 (blacklist bypass, low impact since blacklist is a soft anti-spam/policy control, not an authorization boundary).

packages/emails/src/templates/OrganizerAddGuestsEmail.tsx and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail.tsx — guest-supplied email/name strings are rendered through React JSX components (auto-escaping), so no XSS/HTML-injection was found in the new email templates; zod's `z.string().email()` on the `guests` field (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5) rejects embedded whitespace/CRLF, so no email-header-injection vector was found via the guests array — confidence 75, severity informational (no finding, stated for completeness per instructions).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` does not log the caught error object, guest emails, or booking id, so no PII/secret leakage occurs here, but this also means failures are effectively unobservable/undebuggable in production — confidence 100, severity informational (no security finding).

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking is fetched with prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, include: ... }) and no caller-scoping predicate (e.g., userId/teamId/org/tenant) is applied in the query itself. Authorization is enforced only afterward via imperative checks (isTeamAdminOrOwner/isOrganizer/isAttendee). That matches the finding’s concern about lack of an invariant in the query shape; however, since a permission check does exist before any mutation, this is more a defense-in-depth/maintainability security hardening issue than a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the blacklist is derived inside the request handler via `process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS ? process.env.BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(",").map(...) : []`, which means the env string is parsed on every mutation call. This is a diff-grounded performance/configuration concern (and makes the blacklist inherently process-wide rather than per-tenant), but it is not a direct correctness/security defect shown by the diff.

(confidence 50, severity P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the diff shows `EventManager` being instantiated with an object composed at the call site via `{ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }`, where `user` is `ctx.user` and `credentials` come from a separate `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` call. This is indeed an ad-hoc assembly that relies on `ctx.user`’s shape and on `EventManager`’s expected constructor input staying compatible; the spread/override also means any existing `user.credentials` would be silently shadowed. The diff doesn’t prove a runtime failure today, but it is a concrete maintainability/type-contract concern introduced in this new handler.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler loads `booking` (including `attendees`) once, computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering against that in-memory `booking.attendees`, and then performs a separate `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` write. The diff shows no transaction/locking or re-check at write time, so two concurrent calls could both pass the dedup check based on the same pre-update snapshot and attempt to insert the same attendee email(s). However, the finding’s stronger claim that there is “no unique constraint or schema-level invariant” cannot be verified from this diff (Prisma schema/indexes are not shown), so the outcome (duplicate rows vs. a DB constraint error) isn’t fully provable from the provided changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterating over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sending an email to each attendee (packages/emails/email-manager.ts).
